mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) consistently reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0% (the current level), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 1.0% signals imminent monetary tightening that raises corporate borrowing costs and reduces earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises above 1.0% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days through joint series behavior.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS up and UNRATE down) fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window, or the interaction term Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1.2 million units signal overheating consumer demand and potential Fed policy response, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1.2 million units.

mechanism_narrative: Higher industrial production (INDPRO) levels indicate robust manufacturing growth that supports corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days without regime-specific conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding $475 billion signals strong consumer spending momentum that drives positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days through immediate demand effects.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS exceeds 475,000 million dollars.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rates (UNRATE) falling below 4.0% indicate a tight labor market that accelerates wage inflation and forces premature monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1.0% correlates with reduced equity valuations due to higher discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.0%.
